editorial:
Ever feel like your life is stuck on repeat? Wesley Gibson knows exactly how you feel. He's a bored office worker with a cheating girlfriend and a boss who walks all over him. Then one day, a mysterious woman named Fox shows up and tells him his father was a legendary assassin. Suddenly, Wesley is pulled into a secret group called the Fraternity, where he learns to bend bullets and tap into hidden powers. The movie has a wild, over-the-top energy that grabs you right from the start. It's loud, flashy, and doesn't take itself too seriously. You'll find yourself rooting for Wesley as he goes from nobody to badass.

The action scenes are the real star here. The bullet-bending sequences and crazy stunts are shot with style and speed. James McAvoy does a great job showing Wesley's transformation, and Angelina Jolie brings cool confidence to Fox. The pacing rarely slows down, which keeps things exciting. On the downside, the story can feel a bit thin, and some of the violence is pretty intense. If you're looking for deep meaning, this isn't it. But if you want pure, adrenaline-fueled fun, you'll have a blast. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final act, Wesley discovers that Sloan has been lying. The Fraternity doesn't actually get orders from Fate. Sloan has been making up targets to kill people for money and power. Wesley also learns that his father was actually killed by Cross, who was trying to protect Wesley from Sloan. In the end, Wesley turns the tables on Sloan. He uses his bullet-bending skills to take out the Fraternity members who betrayed him. Sloan tries to escape but Wesley shoots him from a long distance. Wesley then walks away, finally in control of his own life and destiny.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves high-energy action movies with a rebellious streak.
